mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior 3 months signals monetary easing, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined by at least 0.1% over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE has increased by >0.3pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a contraction in real GDP (GDPC1) over the prior 3 months indicates a severe economic slowdown, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate profitability.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO change < -0.5% and GDPC1 change < -0.2% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO and GDPC1 both decline by >0.5% and >0.2% respectively over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market boom (HOUST > 1400), rising home construction activity signals strong consumer confidence and increased disposable income, which fuels corporate revenue growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST > 1400.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the prior 3 months indicates robust labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS has increased by at least 0.1% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 208.0, it signals accelerating inflation, which triggers a monetary policy tightening by the Federal Reserve, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 208.0.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 208.0) and elevated interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, which increases the cost of capital and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 208.0 and FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of industrial production contraction (INDPRO < 100), manufacturing slowdowns reduce corporate output and profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 100.
